# Design

Nine requirements, three fronts, new code in new files so the merges are mechanical. Front one, find (src/grep.c, src/files.c, src/walk.c): grep takes trigrams from the pattern, asks body_tri for candidate file ids under the branch predicate branch_scope_sql already builds, scans the candidates from disk with regexec or memmem in parallel workers, maps each hit line onto the symbol spans of its file (one query per candidate file, cached), ranks by the rules in req 1 and prints under a budget with the same omitted-count tail cg context uses; files answers from files joined with file_fts and a symbol count subquery; the filters are one shared Filter struct parsed in main and applied in rank_query, context, survey and grep; walk.c spreads the top-level directories over a thread pool, each thread walking with readdir d_type and the shared Ignore, results merged and sorted; the git-assisted pass asks gitint for the porcelain status and the diff against the recorded head and feeds the paths through the existing targeted-walk path; the contentless FTS tables, body_tri, file_fts and files.base land in schema 18 with a meta fts_mode key. Front two, presence (src/plugin.c, src/native.c): plugin.c renders the marketplace tree from string templates and the cg path, and integrate.c's apply, detect and doctor call it; native.c owns cg hook event, the native rows in agents (schema 18 adds the columns), the pending-spawn matching, worktree detection through cg_find_root_at and git_head, task attribution, the agent.native.* events, and cg fleet discover over the transcript helper lifted out of recap.c; fleet_status and fleet tree read the native rows beside the fleet ones, and fleet.js grows a Sessions root fed by the tree JSON. Front three, projection (src/projection.c, src/conflicts.c): projection.c selects the branch set from the registry and the agents table, writes shadow commits with a copied index, folds with merge-tree, writes the ref and the projections row, and optionally checks out and indexes the projection worktree; conflicts.c computes the symbol, interface and near findings from git diff hunks and the graph's per-branch symbol spans, diffs them against projection_findings, emits the events and steers through driver_steer; the triggers are a dirty note under .codegraph plus a forked background build, called from the post-edit hook, cg hook event, watch, serve and the supervisor. Front four, the fleet shape (src/fleet.c, src/orchestrate.c): the manager role's templates expand {wave} and the worker role's expand {task}, so the defaults give one manager per wave on wave/{feature}/{wave} cut from main and one worker per task on task/{feature}/{task} cut from the wave branch; a template without the placeholder keeps the old one-per-feature or one-per-wave shape, which is how existing configurations keep working; the supervisor holds an array of managers instead of one, spawns a worker for every task its slots allow, and under [hierarchy] waves = parallel starts a task whose requires are still open with a prompt that points it at the projection, keeps the done gate strict, and after a wave lands merges main forward into the live wave branches and steers their workers to cg fleet sync. Merge discipline for the parallel waves: cg.h additions go in one labelled block per task at the end of the file; main.c gets one else-if per new command; help.c one table block per command; mcp.c one TOOLS entry per tool; db.c appends its schema strings with a comment naming the task; nobody reformats a file they did not create.
